remainingBoundaries: Raw REST bodyBytes, content-length and member-order layout were not retained; the record proves decoded response semantics, not wire layout.
The closure review and the final-artifact regression are separate conditions and stay open.
The artifact is the strict profile of the commit named; a later source change needs a new replay.

Held writers: production refused a writer held behind a read lock with ABORTED after about 20.6 s (REST and gRPC, both recordings, measured from dispatch to answer and including the worker's own start-up of about 1 s); strict waits 20 s, so a replay of the writer rows judges that a held writer is refused, not the exact second. The writer order rows record whether a writer answered before or after its anchor was sent.

Read-time retention: the replay's database is younger than the read time asked for, so the clock is advanced once (3700 s, hidden from the recording) after the other chains, and the 59 and 61 minute reads are judged by accepted/refused class (a read at a time before a document existed answers not-found, which is accepted); production's database was older than the hour and the replay's is not, so a found document is compared only when both sides found one.
Token validation: P14 observes malformed (REST) and unknown tokens; P16 records foreign-project and foreign-database uses, and P01 records finished-token uses.
